subject: Segmentation needs for MedShift — follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Khanna <aisha.k@medshift.com>, Procurement <procurement@medshift.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Segmentation needs for MedShift — follow-up & next steps

Hi Aisha / MedShift team,

Thanks for the time today — useful to hear more about your clinical assistant use case and the constraints around PHI. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next steps list so we can qualify the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem):

Summary of what we heard:
- Workload: short clinical summarization requests + real-time assistant queries, average request ~150 tokens input, responses ~120 tokens.
- Traffic pattern: steady baseline with daily peaks (EHR sync windows) — you estimated ~60–120 reqs/s peak.
- Compliance: PHI-in-scope, preference for VPC or dedicated isolation, SOC2 + HIPAA required.
- SLOs: target p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms (token-level latency), and 99.9% availability for core assistant endpoints.

Primary decision points we need from you to qualify options:
1) Confirm whether persistent KV caching across requests is acceptable (this affects Dedicated caching benefits).
2) Clarify max concurrent sessions during peak 15-minute window (gives us autoscale sizing).
3) Procurement: preferred term length (12/24/36 months) and whether a standard BAA is required now or during contract negotiation.

Our initial guidance (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to start; we'd recommend only if you can accept multi-tenant with VPC peering and strong contractual controls.
- Dedicated: good trade-off for predictable performance + reserved capacity; reduces multi-tenant variability and gives you control over instance sizing.
- Private VPC / On-prem: required if you must keep networking fully customer-managed or have strict data locality / HSM/KMS requirements.

Attachments: I’ve attached an SLA-comparison workbook that maps typical performance profiles and recommended reserved capacity sizes for your traffic band. Also included a simple network-template PDF we use to speed up VPC discussions.

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm concurrent peak number + whether on-prem is mandatory or just preferred.
- Us: build a short pilot proposal (Dedicated pilot sizing + success criteria) and a draft commercial outline.

Can we schedule a 30-minute follow-up early next week to lock down concurrent peak and procurement timelines? I’m available Mon/Tue afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

----
Attachment stubs: SLA-comparison.xlsx (spreadsheet), network-template.pdf (diagram)

From: Dr. Aisha Khanna <aisha.k@medshift.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medshift.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segmentation needs for MedShift — follow-up & next steps

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the clear recap — confirming a few datapoints from our side so you can size the pilot: we typically hit ~90 reqs/s sustained during the morning sync and spikes up to ~140 reqs/s for short bursts (2–5 minutes) when multiple clinicians open patient notes after rounds. Average token sizes you called out look right.

Important constraints:
- This is PHI; HIPAA-compliant deployment is mandatory.
- We need p99 at the request level (end-to-end) to remain under ~350ms; if that requires dedicated capacity during core hours, we are open to that.
- We cannot permit offloading of raw PHI to third-party storage unless encrypted with our KMS keys.

Procurement note (cc’d): we will require a redline on liability limits and want to see your standard BAA. Also share SOC2 Type II report and any pen-test summary you can provide.

For next steps: please send a short pilot plan (what reserved capacity you recommend, measurable success criteria, and whether autoscaling can be configured for the initial pilot). Also share a proposed timeline and ballpark pricing for a 30–60 day pilot.

Best,
Aisha
Chief Product Officer
MedShift Health

----
Quoted earlier: "Thanks for the time today — useful to hear more about your clinical assistant use case..."

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Khanna <aisha.k@medshift.com>, Procurement <procurement@medshift.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segmentation needs for MedShift — follow-up & next steps

Aisha — thanks for the confirmation and the constraints. Quick response with a proposed pilot approach and internal asks (looping Monica and Markus to pull commercial/tech).

Pilot proposal (short):
- Mode: Dedicated reserved capacity for 60 days with autoscale headroom for 2x burst. This gives predictable p99 latency while we validate cache and batching behavior. If after pilot you require customer-managed networking and KMS we will transition the deployment to Private VPC.
- Sizing: start with a single reserved pool equivalent to 8 A100-class GPUs (we recommend starting there based on your peak ~140 reqs/s with the token sizes mentioned). We will right-size after a short 7-day load observation window.
- Success criteria: p99 end-to-end <= 350ms for 95% of 7-day observation; throughput sustaining 120 reqs/s with <= 10% variance; no PHI leakage and keys managed per your KMS requirements if we transition to VPC.
- Timeline: proposal + SOW draft within 3 business days; pilot provisioning within 5 business days after SOW sign; observation window 7–14 days.
- Pricing: ballpark estimate for 60-day pilot with reserved capacity + support = USD 45k–70k depending on GPU class and ingress egress profile; final pricing in SOW.

Monica / Markus — can you draft the SOW and attach the SOC2 summary and BAA template for MedShift review? I added a short commercial placeholder doc to the attachments.

Action items recap:
- MedShift: confirm whether on-prem is strictly required or if Private VPC is acceptable as a next-step; provide procurement contact.
- Redwood: draft SOW + commercial and attach compliance artifacts (SOC2, pen-test summary, BAA).

I’m scheduling a 30-minute follow-up for Tue 2027-04-06 10:00 PT; if that works for you I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Vivek
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

----
Attachment stubs: proposal-draft.docx (word), SLA-comparison.xlsx (spreadsheet), network-template.pdf (diagram)

Quick note from ops/commercial — we’ve uploaded a short commercial placeholder and a SOC2 summary to the Drive link Vivek included. Procurement, can you please confirm the contracting contact and whether you prefer a week-to-week pilot signature or a short SOW + order form?

Aisha — if Private VPC is acceptable as a post-pilot path, we’ll include the KMS/HSM appendix in the SOW so your security team can review before the pilot starts.

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for Tue 2027-04-06 10:00 PT.
